Chapter 7: Navigating Setbacks—Learning and Adapting When Things Go Wrong.
Even with the best system in place, we all face setbacks. Life just throws things our way—stress, getting sick, travel, or those completely unexpected curveballs. All of these can shake up your routines and really put your resolve to the test.
But here’s the thing: what really matters isn’t whether you slip up. It’s how you handle those moments when things don’t go as planned. That’s what separates a quick stumble from falling off track for good.
Picture this—making a change is a lot like steering a boat across a lake. Sometimes the wind or a strong current nudges you off course. The key isn’t to panic or give up. Instead, you make a few small adjustments, keep your eye on where you’re headed, and keep moving forward.
So, how do you actually navigate those inevitable setbacks?
First, let’s normalize them. Expect that you’ll have lapses now and then. Slipping up isn’t a sign of weakness—it’s just part of the process when you’re trying to change.
Next, instead of beating yourself up, take a step back and analyze what happened. What was going on right before the slip? Were there certain triggers, or maybe some support or structure was missing?
From there, think about how you can adjust your system. Maybe you need to tweak your environment, switch up your routines, or lean a little more on your support network. Even tiny tweaks can make a big difference in avoiding the same setback next time.
For example, imagine you’re trying to stop late-night snacking, but you notice it always happens after stressful days. Instead of just telling yourself “don’t snack,” what if you tried adding a new stress-relief habit, like taking a walk or calling a friend? Suddenly, you’re tackling the root cause, not just the symptom.
And you know what else is crucial? Practicing self-compassion. It’s so easy to fall into harsh self-criticism, but that just drains your motivation and makes it harder to get back on track. Try treating yourself the way you’d treat a friend—acknowledge that it’s tough, give yourself credit for the progress you’ve made, and focus on what you can do next.
So, here’s the key takeaway: setbacks aren’t failures—they’re feedback. If you approach them with curiosity and a flexible mindset, every obstacle becomes a chance to learn and grow.
